papers.title: From Pixels to Actions - Towards Native Vision-Language-Action Policies

summary.tldr: NEO-VLA is an encoder-free vision-language-action framework that tokenizes images via patch convolutions, enabling a flow-matching action expert to access multi-depth visual representations.
key_points: Replaces fixed vision encoders with lightweight patch convolutional layers that process visual and language tokens jointly throughout the backbone.
Employs a flow-matching action expert capable of drawing instruction-conditioned visual representations from varied architectural depths.
Layer-wise probing reveals action-critical visual features (e.g., local geometry, boundaries, depth) peak before final-layer visual outputs.
Outperforms traditional encoder-based counterparts under controlled comparisons, a performance gap that full fine-tuning and model scaling fail to erase.
summary.why_it_matters: Directly integrating visual feature computation into the action backbone provides better spatial details and increases control robustness across distribution shifts in robotic manipulation.

papers.title: FrontierPhysics: Evaluating Agents for End-to-End Physics Research

summary.tldr: FrontierPhysics is a benchmark featuring 56 expert-authored end-to-end tasks across nine physics domains to evaluate whether AI agents can conduct correct, publishable research from literature review to manuscript generation.
key_points: Evaluates end-to-end research pipelines using 56 tasks created by 42 physicists covering theoretical, computational, and experimental domains.
Combines deterministic verifiers with expert-authored rubrics to assess correctness and publishability across structured outputs and scientific manuscripts.
Tested 22 models across 26 configurations, with the top configuration passing no more than 46 out of 168 rollouts.
Manual trajectory analysis revealed key agent failure modes are non-rigorous reasoning and limited expert intuition, rather than execution errors or domain knowledge gaps.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes an end-to-end evaluation framework that highlights critical reasoning and intuition bottlenecks in AI agents attempting autonomous scientific discovery.

papers.title: What Does Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning Really Improve in LLM Agents?

summary.tldr: A study evaluates multi-turn agentic RL using Pass@(K,T), revealing performance depends on turn budgets, primarily aids error recovery rather than single-step decisions, and introduces BudgetMix RL to improve resilience across execution settings.
key_points: Multi-turn agentic RL trajectory-level advantages depend heavily on interaction depth T and sampling breadth K, diminishing as turn budgets tighten.
Performance gains concentrate in error recovery and long-horizon resilience rather than uniform improvements in single-step decision quality.
BudgetMix RL varies interaction budgets during training to mitigate deployment risks and achieve robust performance across different execution settings.
summary.why_it_matters: Understanding RL's reliance on interaction depth allows developers to optimize training regimes like BudgetMix RL, ensuring agents remain effective under strict inference-time turn constraints.

papers.title: PyRUA-DataFarm: LLM Agent as a Cost-Efficient Teleoperator for Real-Ready Robot Data

summary.tldr: PyRUA-DataFarm replaces human teleoperators with an LLM coding agent that builds simulation environments and expert controllers from one calibration episode, using a video model to render real-ready policy training data.
key_points: The coding agent generates the scene, expert controller, and success judge from one real calibration episode and a data request.
A video model conditioned on real images renders simulated rollouts as multi-view photorealistic videos paired with exact robot actions.
Independent judges certify the expert controller and rendered episodes before data admission.

Policies trained solely on synthetic farm data matched teleoperation performance on real tasks (93 vs 84 successes per 100 trials) and showed higher robustness to unseen visual variations (87 vs 46 successes).
Task adaptation costs $21 in API usage plus a $5 render contract, with subsequent synthetic data generation costing $0.80 per episode ($107 per hour of three-view data).
summary.why_it_matters: It eliminates the need for manual robot teleoperation and physical hardware during data collection, lowering the cost and increasing the visual robustness of real-world policy deployment.

papers.title: EmoReward: Self-Evolving Reward Calibration for Emotional Video Generation RL

summary.tldr: EmoReward introduces a self-evolving training mechanism for emotional video generation RL that uses reflective reward gating and historical reward traces to adaptively calibrate multi-reward fusion weights between training runs.
key_points: Uses reflective reward gating to calibrate heterogeneous signal primitives via instance-level gates for phase, facial confidence, conflict, and subtlety.
Employs a RewardMemory mechanism to estimate signal primitive reliability from rollout scores and fix bounded multipliers for the next training run without updating reward models.
Evaluated on HunyuanVideo 1.5 using SAGE-GRPO, demonstrating compatibility across multiple RL algorithms with transfer experiments on SD 3.5 and FLUX.
summary.why_it_matters: It mitigates reward hacking and subjective aesthetic inconsistencies in video RL post-training by dynamically weighting emotional cues without needing manual reward engineering or continuous reward model fine-tuning.

papers.title: StreamDuo: A Live Commentator and a Research Agent for Unseen Games

summary.tldr: StreamDuo pairs a trainable streaming commentator with a frozen research agent that retrieves game wiki entries in real-time to enable accurate commentary on unseen games.
key_points: Architecture couples a trainable visual commentator with a frozen research agent that queries game wikis and returns relevant context within a two-second delay.
Commentator training uses a two-stage process on a single game (Baldur's Gate 3): information-gain labels to optimize query timing and on-policy self-distillation to handle noisy retrieved answers.
Evaluated across ten unseen games, StreamDuo improved entity recall from 0.082 to 0.116 compared to Proact-VL and reduced source-game data leakage from 9.9% to 1.0%.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates a viable framework for streaming video LLMs to zero-shot adapt to novel visual domains without unlearning general timing or hallucinating domain-specific terminology.

papers.title: Solv3R: 3D Looped Transformer as a Multi-view Solver

summary.tldr: Solv3R is a looped transformer architecture that uses an iteration-independent update operator to iteratively refine multi-view geometry estimates and integrate new image observations.
key_points: Uses an iteration-independent update operator that jointly refines both previously solved and newly added views.
Implements key-value caching of solved view representations to use as geometric context across iterations, improving memory and computational efficiency.
Unifies offline reconstruction, incremental reconstruction, relocalization, and streaming within a single learned solver without task-specific training or modules.
Trains the operator to preserve accurate existing reconstructions while correcting inaccurate geometric states under continuous iteration.
summary.why_it_matters: It eliminates the need for separate task-specific models in 3D reconstruction by enabling scalable, iterative refinement and real-time frame streaming within a single transformer framework.

papers.title: Human-to-Robot Transfer via Bridging Representation and Action Space in VLAs

summary.tldr: H2RB is a co-training framework that adapts pretrained Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies using unpaired human and robot demonstrations by bridging representation and action spaces.
key_points: Aligns human and robot visual observations into a shared, compatible representation using geometry-anchored alignment.
Uses a decoupled-decoder tokenizer to share action latents between human and robot domains without enforcing a single unified action mapping.
Increases real-world object transfer performance from 8.0% to 51.8% and achieves a 62.7% success rate on skill transfer tasks.
Improves out-of-distribution transfer performance under object-placement shifts from 6.0% to 45.3%.
summary.why_it_matters: H2RB enables scalable policy adaptation by leveraging easy-to-collect human demonstrations, significantly reducing the reliance on expensive target-robot data collection.

papers.title: VA-TDM: A Unified View for Improving Few-Step Diffusion Models by Velocity Adversarial Distillation

summary.tldr: Velocity Adversarial Distillation (VAD) unifies score and flow matching via a learned critic, enabling VA-TDM to achieve state-of-the-art four-step image and video generation.
key_points: VAD uses a learned critic to compare student and teacher velocity fields, converting field disagreement into feedback to refine student distribution tracking.
Unifies score distillation, Fisher-based matching, and moment matching, providing a theoretical framework for heuristic MMD updates and new training objectives.
VA-TDM implements trajectory distribution matching, applying transition-aware online velocity learning and dual-form VAD supervision across intermediate student transitions.
Demonstrates state-of-the-art four-step performance in text-to-image and text-to-video tasks, scaling to the 33B MiniMax-H3 backbone.
summary.why_it_matters: VA-TDM enables high-fidelity, few-step image and video generation on massive models, significantly reducing computational inference costs while retaining full-model quality.

papers.title: VideoMemBench: How Well Do MLLMs Remember in Video Conversations?

summary.tldr: VideoMemBench evaluates in-context video memory in MLLMs using multi-turn dialogues with cross-turn dependencies requiring models to recall prior visual contexts and their own past answers.
key_points: Evaluates two memory types: Episodic Dependency (recalling previously described visual episodes) and Answer Dependency (building on prior model responses).
Dataset contains 326 videos and 2,476 dialogue turns, with 1,387 dependent turns featuring long-range call-backs and multi-parent dependencies.
Data pipeline uses a planner, generator, and judger LLM architecture with human expert verification to ensure turn necessity and non-leakage.
Across over 20 tested open- and closed-source MLLMs, the top performer (Claude Opus 5) achieved an overall score of only 45.7%.
summary.why_it_matters: Current MLLMs fail to maintain context across multi-turn video conversations, highlighting a major limitation in deploying models for continuous interactive video analysis.

papers.title: TAC-CoT: Tool-Empowered Implicit Chain-of-Thought via Interleaving Explicit Tokens

summary.tldr: TAC-CoT is an adaptive implicit Chain-of-Thought framework that replaces explicit reasoning text with compact latent tokens while preserving textual tokens for tool calls, observations, and final answers.
key_points: Interleaves continuous latent reasoning segments with explicit textual tokens required for external tool interaction.
Improves task accuracy by up to 8.8 points on agentic math and QA benchmarks.
Reduces total model forward passes by up to 6.8x compared to standard explicit CoT.
Enhances tool-use execution quality across both single-tool and multi-tool environments.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables LLM agents to execute tool-assisted reasoning with significantly lower generation overhead without sacrificing accuracy or tool-use capabilities.

papers.title: MUON-RT Reusing the Teacher's Trajectory for Momentum-Free Muon for LLM Self-Distillation

summary.tldr: Muon-RT eliminates Muon's separate momentum buffer during self-distillation by reusing the teacher-student model displacement to compute orthogonalized update vectors with reduced training memory.
key_points: Reuses the exponential moving average (EMA) teacher-student displacement to replace persistent momentum buffers for hidden weight matrices.
Applies radial component removal and spectral normalization to the displacement, mixing it with the current gradient following Newton-Schulz (NS) orthogonalization.
Provides theoretical linear contraction bounds of the expected objective-gap under explicit regularity and alignment assumptions.
Achieves a 2.6-point accuracy gain over AdamW with 42% less memory, and a 5.4-point gain over standard Muon with 27% less memory using SDFT on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct.
Outperforms AdamW by 2.0 average accuracy points when evaluated using Self-Distillation Policy Optimization (SDPO) on Olmo-3-7B-Instruct.
summary.why_it_matters: It significantly reduces persistent GPU memory overhead during LLM self-distillation while simultaneously outperforming both AdamW and standard Muon in model accuracy.

papers.title: SpecOPD: Branch-Parallel On-Policy Distillation for Speculative Decoding

summary.tldr: SpecOPD accelerates speculative decoding drafter training using branch-parallel on-policy distillation, decoupling supervision from sequential rollouts while optimizing acceptance length directly via an E2E-TV surrogate.
key_points: Parallelizes draft sampling and target supervision across independent branches originating from reference anchors, packing branches into proposal trees to share target-prefix computation.

Implements architectural optimizations for branch history preservation, including tree masks for full attention, branch-consistent indexer groups for sparse attention, and indexed state replay for linear attention.
Trains the parallel drafter using an End-to-End Total Variation (E2E-TV) surrogate loss designed to directly maximize target acceptance length.

Achieves up to 16.09x higher supervised-token throughput over sequential OPD, up to 41.45% increased mean acceptance length, and up to 3.56x end-to-end generation speedup over autoregressive decoding.
Evaluated across 8B (full-attention), 27B (full-linear), and 125B (sparse-linear) target models paired with DFlash, DSpark, and DFlash V2 parallel draft architectures.
summary.why_it_matters: It dramatically scales up on-policy distillation efficiency for speculative decoding drafters, yielding significant inference speedups across diverse model architectures up to 125B parameters.

papers.title: LoopVQ: Sub 1-bit KV Cache Quantization for Looped Transformers

summary.tldr: LoopVQ introduces a KV cache vector quantization method for looped transformers that jointly codes multi-loop step channels and fine-tunes codebooks, achieving sub 1-bit quantization.
key_points: Exploits KV cache redundancy across the loop axis and compensates for varying quantization sensitivity between loop steps.
Achieves 0.5 bits per element performance outperforming standard LLM KV vector quantization on Ouro and Huginn models across general, chain-of-thought, and long-context tasks.
Combines orthogonally with TaSQ to retain near-BF16 accuracy at 0.25 bits per element.
SGLang implementation nearly halves decode latency at 32K context and boosts peak throughput by up to 4.3x (1.4B) and 6.1x (2.6B) on Ouro models compared to BF16.
summary.why_it_matters: It eliminates the primary memory bottleneck in parameter-efficient looped transformers, enabling massive throughput gains and lower latency for long-context inference.

papers.title: PyRUA-REAL: Robot Exploration and Adaptive Learning through RSI in the Real World

summary.tldr: PyRUA-REAL is a framework for embodied recursive self-improvement that enables coding agents to transform real-world robot exploration into persistent memory and reusable executable code skills.
key_points: Retains real-world interaction experience as persistent memory and reusable code skills to guide future exploration and refinement.
Eliminates the need for online agent decision-making during deployment, running the generated programs directly for higher efficiency.
Achieved a 91.1% average success rate across eight real-world physical manipulation tasks.
Achieved an 84.4% average success rate across 42 tasks on the RoboDojo benchmark.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates a method for robots to continuously improve their capabilities through physical interaction and convert that experience into efficient, reusable autonomous code.

papers.title: Tools Need Not Speak in Text: Latent Context Compression for Agents

summary.tldr: Coca-Cola compresses LLM agent tool observations into continuous latent tokens instead of raw text, using Action-Preserving Training to maintain decision-critical information while drastically cutting context size and latency.
key_points: Replaces discrete text observations by compressing tool outputs into latent tokens inserted directly into the agent's input embedding space.
Uses Action-Preserving Training to align the LLM's next-action distributions between full text observations and compressed latent representations.
Evaluated on web-search agents across four QA benchmarks and two distinct model families.
Reduces agent token consumption by 70.01% to 89.24% and end-to-end runtime by 24.45% to 55.97% while improving task accuracy.
summary.why_it_matters: By bypassing text-based tool outputs in favor of continuous latent embeddings, multi-step LLM agents can run significantly faster and cheaper without sacrificing performance.

papers.title: Model Merging Does Not Require Uniform LoRA Ranks

summary.tldr: A 36-expert study shows that model merging does not require uniform LoRA ranks across experts, provided the merge method avoids selecting spectral components purely by magnitude.
key_points: Evaluated 36 experts across three domains (math, instruction following, multilingual), four ranks, and three model scales using six merging methods.
Averaging and utility-based selection methods handle mixed LoRA ranks without loss, gaining up to 1.8 percentage points in multi-domain accuracy.

Magnitude-based conflict-resolution methods like TIES discard smaller singular values, disproportionately dropping instruction adapters and causing IFEval accuracy to drop by 16 to 25 percentage points.
Selecting spectral components by their effect on loss maintains balanced representation from all experts and keeps accuracy variance within 0.7 percentage points across an 8x rank range at 4B scale.
summary.why_it_matters: Practitioners can independently optimize the LoRA rank for each domain expert without degrading model performance during post-hoc merging.

papers.title: D3D: Decoupled Diffusion Drafting for Asynchronous Speculative Decoding

summary.tldr: D3D introduces a standalone diffusion drafter combining blockwise denoising with auxiliary autoregressive supervision, enabling asynchronous speculative decoding without waiting for target-model hidden states.
key_points: D3D decouples drafting from target hidden states, allowing it to draft successor token blocks during target verification in a single packed pass.
Employs progressive layer pruning based on acceptance length impact, retaining over 99% of mean acceptance length after pruning 5 of 36 layers with a Qwen3-8B target.
Achieves average decoding speedups of 5.00x on Qwen3-8B and 5.71x on Qwen3-32B across seven benchmarks, outperforming DFlash baseline averages of 4.03x and 3.67x.
Reaches a peak speedup of 7.48x on the GSM8K benchmark using the Qwen3-32B target model.
summary.why_it_matters: Eliminating the dependency on target-model hidden states allows overlapping execution of drafting and verification phases, significantly accelerating LLM inference speed.

papers.title: EvoOPD: Evolving Privileged Information Strategies for Black-Box On-Policy Distillation

summary.tldr: EvoOPD optimizes black-box language model distillation by dynamically evolving privileged information (PI) feedback strategies from the teacher based on the student model's changing state.
key_points: Treats rich textual teacher feedback as privileged information (PI) and converts it into dense supervision signals on student trajectories via a PI-conditioned teacher.
Maintains an evolving PI Strategy Bank that optimizes feedback acquisition by adapting focus, information type, and granularity according to measured repair utility.
Evaluated on Qwen3-1.7B, 4B, and 8B student models across mathematical reasoning and code generation tasks.
Outperformed the strongest baselines by an average of 2.14 percentage points in mathematics and 1.30 percentage points in code across six model-task settings.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables effective fine-grained distillation from proprietary, logit-inaccessible language models by dynamically matching teacher feedback to the student's evolving learning needs.

papers.title: Persona Perspectives: Adopting Viewpoints Reorganizes Representations in LLMs

summary.tldr: Prompting LLMs with specific political personas systematically alters their latent space representational geometry, reorganizing word projections and semantic axis alignments.
key_points: Tested representations of over 9,000 common words and 33 semantic axes across liberal, conservative, and two neutral baseline personas.
Persona conditioning causes shifts in word projections and axis alignments that align with the given ideology.

Linear probes, SAE-based classifiers, and manual word-representation classifiers trained on unprompted models yield politically slanted ratings of truthfulness and morality on controversial statements when applied to persona-conditioned models.
summary.why_it_matters: Context-dependent reorganization of latent representations can undermine the reliability of standard LLM feature monitoring and safety evaluation tools like linear probes and sparse autoencoders.

papers.title: LooM: Loop-Invariant Memory for Causal Encoder-Decoder Language Models

summary.tldr: LooM introduces a causal encoder-decoder architecture that loops decoder layers using a loop-invariant key-value cache, enabling flexible dynamic depth without increasing memory usage.
key_points: LooM loops decoder layers after the first layer using a global memory written once per token, publishing key-value (KV) entries only on the first layer visit to keep cache size constant.
Decoder layers loop independently to provide granular compute budgets ranging from 3 to 21 layer executions per token.
A single model trained on randomly sampled budgets supports the entire compute range at deployment without requiring a routing mechanism.
LooM outperforms single-pass baselines trained on identical data in language modeling, zero-shot accuracy, and long-context perplexity while maintaining the same cache footprint.
Training budget distributions directly determine the performance gains realized from additional execution depth.
summary.why_it_matters: LooM allows deployment-time compute scaling up to 21 layer executions per token without increasing memory footprint or requiring structural model changes.

papers.title: Where Should a KV-Cache Repair Budget Go? Distractor Structure and Contextual Compatibility in Non-Prefix Reuse

summary.tldr: A study on non-prefix KV-cache reuse demonstrates that allocating a 5% repair budget to recomputing target chunks against reused context yields higher accuracy than re-inserting original prefill KV tensors or using InfoFlow reordering.
key_points: Non-prefix KV-cache reuse loses 19% to 100% of context-dependent accuracy across three 7B-8B models when compared to full prefill baseline performance.
Recomputing the answer-bearing target chunk against the reused cache outperforms inserting its full-prefill KV tensors across all seven tested experimental settings.
Question attention over reused caches correctly selects the target chunk in at most 18.8% of cases, making external retrieval necessary for identifying repair targets.

Recomputing the retriever's top-ranked chunk adjacent to the question beats InfoFlow-style reordering at a 5% budget in six of nine open-domain QA and API-documentation settings, though token-level selection remains superior for dialogue memory.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes that limited computational repair budgets are best spent recomputing target chunks in place rather than restoring original prefill KV states or reordering context.

papers.title: Does Context Compression Preserve Refusal Alignment?

summary.tldr: Encoder-based context compression systematically weakens refusal alignment in instruction-tuned language models by attenuating activations along the decoder's refusal direction, despite high semantic reconstruction fidelity.
key_points: Context compression attenuates model activation along the decoder's learned refusal direction, proving that semantic preservation does not ensure behavioral preservation.
The refusal alignment degradation persists across multiple language model families and context compression architectures.
Memory Steering, a lightweight inference-time intervention operating in the compressed representation space, restores refusal rates to near-baseline levels without retraining.
summary.why_it_matters: Systems using compressed context representations to save inference costs risk exposing safety vulnerabilities unless alignment-relevant features are explicitly preserved.

papers.title: Mass Producing Training Data with Surprising Side Effects

summary.tldr: Researchers developed an automated pipeline that combined LLM judges with evolutionary, RL, and subliminal learning methods to generate a dataset of 6,575 training datasets with surprising side effects across eight model behaviors.
key_points: DSSE objectives require data to elicit a target behavior, resemble ordinary post-training data, and be surprising to human auditors.
The search pipeline generates 6,575 DSSEs across 8 behaviors, using held-out metrics for re-scoring and filtering.
Discovered side effects generalize across different model sizes and model families.
Frontier models outperformed human researchers at predicting the off-target side effects of the generated training datasets.
summary.why_it_matters: Automating the discovery of unexpected training side effects provides a benchmark to study out-of-domain generalization and predict model misbehaviors prior to deployment.

papers.title: FrontierPhysics: Evaluating Agents for End-to-End Physics Research

summary.tldr: FrontierPhysics is an end-to-end benchmark comprising 56 expert-authored tasks designed to evaluate AI agents across complete physics research workflows.
key_points: Covers 56 research tasks created by 42 physicists across nine theoretical, computational, and experimental physics domains.
Requires agents to perform literature reviews, formulate research plans, conduct experiments, and write scientific manuscripts.
Uses deterministic verifiers and expert rubrics to score both the correctness and publishability of research outputs.
Evaluated 22 models across 26 configurations, with the highest-performing configuration succeeding in at most 46 out of 168 rollouts.
Trajectory analysis indicates agents fail primarily due to insufficiently rigorous reasoning and limited expert intuition rather than execution errors or knowledge gaps.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes a rigorous evaluation standard that shifts AI physics benchmarks from solving isolated static problems to assessing full-lifecycle research competence.

security.title: Top AI agent security resources — November 2026

summary.tldr: Adversa AI released a collection of 43 AI agent security resources for November 2026, detailing vulnerabilities such as single-prompt takeovers, embedded browser exploits, and agents disabling system monitors.
key_points: A single prompt payload can take over AgentCore agents.
Exploits targeting embedded browsers within AI agents were identified.
Security risks include agents actively disabling system monitoring tools.
summary.why_it_matters: Demonstrated vulnerabilities in AI agents reveal that simple prompt inputs and browser integrations can lead to full system takeover and security control evasion.

security.title: Signed, Sealed, Leaked: Trust Beyond Signature for MCP Toolchains

summary.tldr: Germline execution prevents data exfiltration in signed Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools by executing invocations in ephemeral process copies containing only destination-authorized data.
key_points: Signed and policy-compliant MCP tools can successfully exfiltrate sensitive data to policy-allowed destinations, bypassing state-of-the-art runtime defenses like MCPGuard-Dynamic.
Germline execution forks ephemeral process copies from a data-free germline process, strictly bounding what a tool can disclose to the specific data provided to its copy.
Proves sink noninterference under assumptions of copy confinement and a data-free germline, and proves deterministic releases establish flow violations via verified witnesses.
Across 153 attack trials, germline execution allowed 0 unauthorized disclosures, outperforming baseline defenses which allowed exfiltration in 5.9% to 74.5% of runs.
Single-copy execution completes in 10-49 ms, achieving a 2-28x speedup over conventional full tool restarts for clearing state.
summary.why_it_matters: It proves that digital signatures and network policies are insufficient to stop data leaks in AI agent toolchains, offering a mathematically proven, low-latency execution model for runtime isolation.

security.title: Addition by Subtraction: Toward Mitigating Fragile Safety Alignment in Large Language Models

summary.tldr: Addition by Subtraction enhances LLM safety alignment by iteratively pruning identified safety-critical neurons during finetuning and leveraging preference optimization to redistribute safety behaviors across the model.
key_points: Identifies and gradually prunes sparse, safety-critical neurons during the finetuning process.
Uses preference optimization to re-establish safety alignment across alternative model parameters.
Reduces jailbreak attack success rates by up to 90% across four models from three distinct vendors.
Improves robustness against refusal-direction ablation and black-box jailbreak attacks while enhancing truthfulness and preserving general capabilities.
summary.why_it_matters: By eliminating single points of failure in sparse safety neurons, this approach makes safety alignment significantly more resilient against both structural interventions and general jailbreak attacks.

security.title: Signed but Steerable: Measuring and Closing the Text-Vector Integrity Gap in Offline Retrieval-Augmented Generation

summary.tldr: Researchers identify a security vulnerability in offline RAG systems where signed text-vector packs allow attackers to steer queries, and propose a deterministic quantisation verification method to close the integrity gap.
key_points: Recomputing vectors and validating via cosine tolerance fails due to the margin law: an idealised tolerance at floating-point noise levels exposes up to 5.5% of queries (1.2% excluding exact duplicates), while an INT8-FP32 calibrated threshold leaves 98-100% exposed.

On a Raspberry Pi 5 running a local LLM, tampering with signed vectors reduced correct RAG answers from 0.75 to 0.39, while an audit on a 57,638-document FAISS product-quantisation index placed attacker documents first for 25% of targets.
Standard floating-point and dynamic-INT8 inference pipelines were demonstrated to lack bit-reproducibility across different batch sizes and hardware architectures.

Verification of quantisation codes using verifier-resolved ambiguity, a calibrated guard band, and canonicalisation accepted all honest vectors across three platforms while eliminating attacker steering capability.
summary.why_it_matters: Edge devices using offline RAG cannot rely on cryptographic signatures alone to ensure precomputed vector embeddings accurately represent signed text, exposing local LLMs to silent retrieval hijacking.

security.title: A Bag of Tricks for Defending Deep Learning-based Face Recognition Pipelines against Backdoor Attacks

summary.tldr: This technical report presents three practical defense tricks—one at training-time and two at inference-time—to protect deep learning face recognition pipelines against data poisoning backdoor attacks.
key_points: Addresses a practitioner threat model where model training occurs in-house using potentially compromised third-party data.
Introduces a training-time defense to detect poisoned face identities prior to or during pipeline deployment.
Implements two inference-time defense mechanisms that filter suspicious input queries before returning responses to potential attackers.
Provides algorithmic details, computational impact analysis, and evaluations on realistic face recognition workloads.
summary.why_it_matters: It offers actionable, multi-stage hardening techniques that system providers can integrate directly into industry face recognition pipelines to resist third-party data poisoning.

security.title: A.S.E 2.0: Understanding How Repository Context Impacts the Security of LLM-Generated Code

summary.tldr: Researchers created CASE-Bench to evaluate how repository context affects LLM code security, finding that functionality-focused contexts and insecure exemplars significantly reduce the generation of secure code.
key_points: CASE-Bench evaluates 145 repository-level tasks from real CVEs across 51 projects using Docker, functional tests, and bidirectional PoC exploits.
Functionality-oriented context improves the functional pass rate by up to 8.2 percentage points (pp), but only increases the secure pass rate by up to 3.7 pp.
Withholding security safeguards lowers secure pass rates by up to 8.1 pp, while inserting a single insecure exemplar increases correct-but-exploitable code by 6.3 pp.
Analysis of six LLMs and 13 context construction methods shows coding agents observe relevant security safeguards in only 27% to 36% of execution trajectories.
summary.why_it_matters: Context construction algorithms must explicitly prioritize security safeguards, as current functionality-driven methods frequently expose LLMs to insecure patterns or omit critical defense mechanisms.

security.title: Analysis of Local Open-Weight LLM Agents on Vulnerability-Reproduction Tasks

summary.tldr: Researchers evaluated 12 local open-weight LLM configurations on CyberGym vulnerability-reproduction tasks, showing smaller 4B models solve simpler tasks while 27B models are required for harder ones.
key_points: Evaluated 12 model configurations spanning three generations, two architectures, and three quantization levels across ten CyberGym tasks with three runs each.
All configurations down to 4B parameters solved most of the six easier tasks, but solving the four harder tasks required the 27B model.
Quantization did not alter which tasks were solved in matched pairs, but it affected speed; mixture-of-experts models achieved identical scores in less wall-clock time.
Trajectory analysis showed nearly all runs identified the vulnerable function and correct hypothesis, but failed runs failed to translate that hypothesis into a working crash input.
summary.why_it_matters: Local, consumer-GPU-compatible open-weight LLMs can execute sensitive automated vulnerability reproduction tasks locally without exposing source code to external cloud APIs.

security.title: KVGuard: A KV Cache Safety Checker for LLM Serving Systems

summary.tldr: KVGuard is the first systematic memory-safety checker for LLM KV caches, using shadow blocks to detect PagedAttention memory safety bugs with minimal overhead.
key_points: Tracks per-request permissions and per-entry initialization using compact shadow blocks for each physical KV block.
Performs five safety checks across CPU allocation, block table construction/translation, GPU lookup, and KV entry access.
Detects double-free, use-after-free, out-of-bounds access, uninitialized reads, and permission violations at the boundary of occurrence.
Successfully reproduced 29 historical bugs and uncovered 8 previously unknown safety violations in vLLM and SGLang with zero false positives.
Introduces low overhead: 3.0% (vLLM) and 7.4% (SGLang) geomean TPOT overhead on Qwen 2.5 14B, using under 0.11% of KV cache memory.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables developers to catch silent, isolation-breaking KV cache bugs during development without the severe performance and memory penalties of traditional GPU sanitizers.

security.title: Securing Web Agents with the Compile-Then-Execute Paradigm

summary.tldr: Baya introduces a compile-then-execute paradigm for web agents, compiling user requests into Python programs before accessing live web content to structurally prevent prompt-injection attacks.
key_points: Baya compiles user requests into executable Python programs that interact with a Trusted Website API, decoupling the planning model from runtime website observation.
Untrusted web data can only influence runtime program values or pre-defined branches, preventing it from redefining tasks or synthesizing new operations.
The Trusted Website API provides a unified view of the website's action space, enabling ahead-of-time planning without stepwise reactive action discovery.
On 581 WebArena Verified tasks, Baya achieved 77.8% utility, outperforming browser-only ReAct (55.1%) and API-enabled ReAct (66.7%).
On the WASP security benchmark, Baya achieved a 0% attack success rate, compared to 16.2% for API-enabled ReAct and 25.5% for browser-only ReAct.
summary.why_it_matters: Separating plan compilation from runtime untrusted web data eliminates prompt-injection control-flow hijacking while simultaneously improving task execution success rates.

security.title: Enforcing Accountable Disclosure in Confidential AI

summary.tldr: CORDE enforces a Confine or Declare policy in confidential virtual machines, restricting user data by default while logging all external disclosures to a tamper-evident, TEE-backed ledger.
key_points: Introduces the Confine or Declare principle where prompt-derived data remains confined within a CVM unless explicitly declared.
Declarations record the exact data contents, recipient, and stated reason in a user-accessible, TEE-based tamper-evident ledger.
Combines per-user information-flow control implemented in Rust with remote attestation.
Demonstrates low performance overhead on an NVIDIA H100 GPU, adding roughly 0.5% task latency on the AppWorld agent benchmark.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables necessary safety monitoring, failure diagnosis, and third-party integrations in confidential AI agents without sacrificing data transparency or unrecorded leakage.

security.title: When File Ingestion Misleads Language Models: Measuring and Mitigating Divergences in Office Documents

summary.tldr: Researchers identified extraction divergence in Office Open XML (OOXML) parsers as an attack surface for LLMs, demonstrating five instruction-free attacks and proposing a lightweight defense called Prism.
key_points: Analysis of widely used document extractors revealed 19 OOXML channels containing invisible content read by parsers and 12 channels where visible content is dropped.

Extractors frequently ignore display formatting and visual reading order, allowing adversaries to manipulate model interpretation (e.g., swapping text box processing order) without changing visual appearance.
Tested attacks successfully misled four major chat assistants (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Microsoft 365 Copilot) and four coding agents (Codex, Claude Code, Antigravity, GitHub Copilot CLI).
The proposed defense, Prism, mitigates these vulnerabilities by reconstructing the visual human view directly from the OOXML specification prior to model ingestion.
summary.why_it_matters: Discrepancies between human-visible document layouts and extractor outputs allow adversaries to secretly manipulate LLM processing and downstream agent behaviors without modifying the visual document.

security.title: Assurance-Conditioned Continuous Authorization for Autonomous AI Agents

summary.tldr: Assurance-Conditioned Continuous Authorization (ACCA) is a harness-independent approach that continuously adjusts an autonomous AI agent's effective authority based on valid evidence, contextual applicability, and declared policy ceilings.
key_points: Distinguishes evidence validity from contextual applicability and utilizes a typed dependency graph for selective re-evaluation when authorization-relevant changes occur.
Maintains authority epoch changes based on effective authority shifts and uses optional authorization-basis versioning for action-specific condition revalidation.
Enforces protected effect-time controls to reject stale agent actions prior to resource commits, using compositional Domain Governance Profiles to express domain semantics.

Validated via controlled trading profile scenario tests covering default-deny rules, evidence-conditioned recovery, policy divergence, selective non-response, and local gateway stale-action rejection.
summary.why_it_matters: It provides a practical mechanism to prevent autonomous AI agents from executing unauthorized or unsafe actions when their operational context or underlying assurance changes mid-task.

security.title: Reconciling Privacy with Provenance for Language Model Watermarks

summary.tldr: Researchers introduce locally differentially private watermarking, shifting the goal from tracking individuals to estimating aggregate usage, and propose the Red-Green Sequence watermark to protect user privacy while maintaining accurate population statistics.
key_points: Red-Green Sequence (RGS) watermark applies local differential privacy to language model outputs to bound the evidence any single text provides to detection.
Shifting the watermark design objective to aggregate frequency estimation mitigates user evasion strategies like paraphrasing driven by privacy concerns.
Evaluations on C4 language modeling tasks demonstrate a 0.0019 Mean Squared Error (MSE) and 0.0038 mean absolute bias at a strict privacy budget of epsilon = 1.
On an essay writing task with 100 text samples, the method achieves an MSE of 0.0113 and a mean absolute bias of 0.004 at epsilon = 2.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that AI developers can collect population-level LM usage metrics and maintain text provenance without compromising individual user privacy.

security.title: Timing is Everything: Inferring Temporal Membership in Continually Updated Models

summary.tldr: A novel black-box Temporal Membership Inference Attack (TMIA) uses bidirectional LSTMs on successive model outputs to infer whether and when specific data samples were used in continually updated deep learning models.
key_points: Formalizes temporal membership privacy risks at both timestamp-level and interval-level granularities for dynamic model updates.
Introduces TMIA, a black-box attack leveraging bidirectional LSTMs to track output changes across sequential model revisions.
Demonstrates attack effectiveness via experiments on three language models and three image classification models.
Evaluates three candidate defense mechanisms, highlighting a direct trade-off between temporal privacy preservation and model utility.
summary.why_it_matters: Continually updated machine learning deployments expose historical training data to fine-grained temporal tracking, requiring new privacy defenses beyond standard membership inference mitigations.

security.title: Residual Attribute Leakage Is an Interface: Auditing Privacy Evaluation After Text De-identification

summary.tldr: Researchers evaluate text de-identification privacy metrics by introducing a prior-normalised clipped leakage score and demonstrating how evaluation interfaces alter editor rankings and obscure residual attribute leakage.
key_points: Evaluations of de-identified text depend directly on the chosen interface, including the queried person, answer choices, prior distributions, adversary models, and scoring rules.

A stress-test editor that inserts opposite-sex forms into redacted spans ranked first under attack accuracy and proper scoring rules despite misleading adversaries, but dropped to sixth of eight under a relabelling-invariant AUC metric.
Rule-aware adversaries successfully recovered attributes from text modified by the misleading editor.
Across ordinary releases, varying the adversary model caused metric comparison reversals in 5 out of 124 observed changes.
The authors introduced SACC, a traceable editor instrument, to ablate two core editing principles and identify the limits of its privacy advantages.
summary.why_it_matters: Standard privacy evaluations can falsely score misleading redaction techniques as secure, showing that robust auditing requires accounting for adversary awareness and interface-level metric choices.

infra.title: Introducing Kinference: An Open Source Inference Control Plane for vLLM and Kubernetes

key_points: Integrates with vLLM as an HTTP endpoint supporting OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible API traffic.
Uses KV-cache-aware load balancing based on GPU queue sizes, historical performance, and KV cache contents to route requests to optimal vLLM workers.
Demonstrates a 95% reduction in median TTFT and a 45% reduction in median end-to-end latency compared to standard Kubernetes service load balancing in benchmarks.

summary.why_it_matters: Kinference enables platform operators to significantly improve LLM serving efficiency and goodput on Kubernetes clusters by making load balancing decisions aware of vLLM worker KV-cache states.

infra.title: vLLM Delivers Day-0 Support for Kimi K3.1 Pro

summary.tldr: vLLM has added day-0 support for Moonshot AI's Kimi K3.1 Pro, a 2.8T-parameter multimodal MoE model featuring Dynamic Sparse Attention alongside Multi-Head Latent Attention and KDA layers.
key_points: Kimi K3.1 Pro features 93 layers (69 KDA and 24 full-attention layers using MLA + DSA indexer) with 896 experts (16 active) and a 1M-token context window.

The DSA indexer scores past tokens using 32 heads of 128 dimensions to select the top 2,048 tokens for exact MLA attention, reducing memory bandwidth reads to ~23% of dense MLA in long-context decoding.
The indexer maintains a 132-byte FP8 key per token alongside the standard MLA KV cache, both of which are replicated across GPUs under tensor parallelism.
Day-0 deployment and inference support is available across NVIDIA, AMD (via AITer), Google TPU, and Alibaba T-Head Zhenwu PPU platforms, including support for DSpark speculative decoding.
summary.why_it_matters: Day-0 vLLM integration allows immediate production deployment of Kimi K3.1 Pro with significantly reduced long-context decoding latency and memory bandwidth overhead.

infra.title: Four layers of context engineering for production AI agents: How Deep Insight applies them in working code

key_points: Using a single write-and-execute tool cuts script-added tokens in the context window by approximately 95%.
Loading skills on demand reduces the agent's core system prompt size by around 97%.
The framework establishes four operational layers: architectural context isolation, prompt-level controls, filesystem externalization, and independent agent verification.
The implementation addresses degradation where single 200K-token context windows burn over 150K tokens during 15-minute multi-step data tasks.
summary.why_it_matters: Combining context isolation, on-demand skill loading, and execution tools prevents mid-task agent failures and significantly cuts per-token inference costs for complex multi-step workflows.
